lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The walk back from the east gate took longer than the morning's survey. The rain that had threatened the lower districts since noon finally broke, not in a clean downpour, but in a thin, greasy mist that turned the dust in the unpaved alleys into gray paste.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg pulled his wool cloak tighter over his shoulders, his boots making a wet, sucking sound in the lane.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: If it keeps up like this, the foundations on the south quarter are going to float before we finish the month.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo said, stepping carefully around a broken drainage tile.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: They're going to settle. Which means the temple will have to pay twice as much for shoring next season. The water's just doing the math for them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon walked between them, her head down, holding her satchel tight against her chest to keep the damp off the paper. Her boots were caked in the same commercial mortar dust Zeek had noticed earlier, the gray residue that didn't match the temple mix.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They reached the room without running into the Collector or anyone else who looked like they had business with them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg dropped the survey rods by the door, unlatched the shutter to let the stale air out, and dropped onto his bench without lighting the lamp. The room went gray as the daylight faded through the unglazed window frame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon didn't sit. She laid her map out on the pine table, smoothing the curled edges of the parchment with the flat of her hand. The four boxes—CLAIMED, COST, LIMIT, and the empty space she'd left after the east wall—were barely visible in the dim light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She picked up her stylus, hovered the metal point over the blank space beside the east-side survey mark, and then stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek set his pack down by the threshold. He didn't take anything out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon kept the stylus steady, though her hand cast a long, shaky shadow across the parchment under the gray light from the window.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't have a name for this box yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo said, leaning against the doorframe while she wrung the mist from the fringe of her shawl.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg let out a short, rough breath that sounded almost like a laugh.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: The city's keeping score. We're just writing down the numbers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek walked over to the table and looked down at the map. The defaced spiral-drop NEEN-soon had drawn in the corner sat right on the boundary line between the east wall and the lower tanneries, as if the same crack ran underneath both of them without caring about the distance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He reached out, took the small ceramic ink-pot by its neck, and moved it two inches to the left, covering the empty space entirely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon looked up at him, her eyes dark in the failing light. For a second she looked like she wanted to argue, to reach for the stylus and scratch the word down anyway before the dark took the room. Then she slowly lowered her hand, the metal point resting against the grain of the wood beside the paper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon said, her voice dropping into a sharper, harder register.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Not after what we saw on the curtain wall. The temple survey codes don't match the commercial stock. That means the records were altered twice—once when the wall went up, and again when they tried to scrape the name out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo pushed off the doorframe, her interest suddenly sharp.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You're saying the east-side survey isn't the whole record.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I'm saying the public registry only shows what the temple wanted kept after the second consolidation,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon said, tapping the edge of her uninked stylus against the table.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: If we want to know whose name was under that defaced seal, we aren't going to find it on the outside of the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The lower archive branch behind the third district weigh-station,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The old tax ledgers from before the plague years. The ones the Collector said stay locked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the ink-pot covering the empty box on the map. He didn't reach for his pack. He didn't look for an excuse to wait.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: If we get to the weigh-station before the evening shift changes, the night clerk won't check the seals on the side bins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stood up, his boots hitting the floorboards with a dull, heavy jar, and reached for his spear. En-KHEH-doo was already sliding her ledger into her pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon picked up her stylus, tucked it behind her ear, and rolled the map tight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They left the room without looking back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The rain had thickened by the time they reached the third district weigh-station.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It stood between a grain warehouse and a public cistern, a low administrative building with a roof pitched just enough to send runoff into the alley. Water streamed from the carved mouths of two clay lions above the entrance. Beneath them, porters waited with wet sacks over their shoulders while a clerk shouted weights through an open window.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The front doors were still busy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek led them around the rear wall, where broken amphorae and discarded tally sticks had collected beneath the eaves. A narrow wooden door sat between two storage bins. Its temple seal had been pressed into a lump of clay at shoulder height.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You said the night clerk wouldn't check it.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I'm beginning to suspect your plans rely heavily on other people being worse at their jobs than you are.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo leaned close to the seal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The impression is sharp, but the edges have started taking damp. Four hours. Six at most.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon removed a small wrapped packet from her satchel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Inside lay three clay seal impressions.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I copied errors made by temple seals.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That answer would not comfort a magistrate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She selected the closest impression and handed it to Zeek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The copied seal matched the clay on the door except for a tiny break in the outer ring.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The third district is not where competent officials are promoted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the front of the building, where another weight was shouted through the rain.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: At last. A weakness in government we can depend on.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not cut through the clay. That would leave an obvious break. Instead, he slid the blade beneath the lump and worked it slowly away from the wood until the entire seal came loose in one piece.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The room beyond smelled of dust, wet rope, and old grain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek pressed the original seal back into place from the inside. It would not survive close inspection, but it might survive indifference.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is not the same answer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The storage room held cracked measuring jars, sacks of outdated weights, and stacks of waxed tally boards tied with cord. Rain drummed against the roof. Voices from the public chamber reached them through the inner wall, flattened into meaningless sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon moved to the far shelves.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The lower ledgers won't be stored with current accounts.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Current records are useful. Old ones are dangerous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg lifted a sack and looked behind it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They found the archive door at floor level behind a stack of broken scales.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was smaller than Zeek expected. A clerk would have to stoop to enter. The bronze lock had been polished recently, though dust covered the surrounding bricks.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The Collector said the drawers stay locked. He didn't say abandoned.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So whoever opens it has the key,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo pressed her thumb against the lower hinge.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Other people being worse at their jobs again?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: This time we owe them thanks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo worked the pin loose with the tip of her knife. BAH-lahg caught the door before it dropped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The space behind it descended three narrow steps into darkness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the mark beneath the linen warm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon saw him flex his hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The archive chamber was long and low, its ceiling supported by cedar beams blackened with age. Clay tablets filled wooden pigeonholes from floor to ceiling. Some were stacked openly. Others sat inside sealed bins marked with year signs and district codes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the far end stood seven narrow drawers fitted into the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked back toward the steps.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon moved among the shelves, reading labels under her breath.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Pre-plague property levy. Grain exemptions. Inheritance disputes. Boundary tax…

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She stopped at a row of tablets bundled in rotted linen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: EAST CURTAIN DISTRICT—PRIVATE HOLDINGS BEFORE CONSOLIDATION
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo took the lamp while NEEN-soon untied the cord.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first tablet listed three warehouse owners.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second recorded a dyer's yard absorbed into temple property.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third had been scraped smooth and reused for grain tallies.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The records changed halfway through the bundle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Private holdings became temple allocations without purchase sums or witness seals.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That is the same thing with a cleaner robe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A narrow ledger tablet lay beneath the others, its face crowded with tax figures. Nothing unusual appeared in the main columns.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But along the left margin, someone had written three smaller lines.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first line was a correction.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second recorded a disputed measure.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: 'Ahm-MAH-roo, son of DAH-gahn EE-lee. Potter by trade. Keeper of the lower cistern stair by hereditary obligation.'

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: 'Property exempt from levy while seventh access remains sealed.'

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The archive seemed to contract around them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One line survived near the lower edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She tilted it into the light.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: 'Exemption revoked after keeper refused transfer of the name.'

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You know what the words mean.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't know what they mean together.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The main text had been written by a formal clerk. Straight wedges. Even spacing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The note about Ahm-MAH-roo was smaller.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Someone added this after the ledger was closed,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Because the official entry no longer did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the seven locked drawers.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then whatever came next is in there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Someone dragged the broken scales away from the archive door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A key entered the bronze lock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon held the ledger tablet against her chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg raised his spear in the dark.
